# Security baseline

<!-- Generated by `cidx security baseline`. Do not edit by hand. -->

What the built-in preset catalogue ships: every container image it runs, pinned
by digest, what those images carry, and every HIGH/CRITICAL finding accepted on
them — with the reason it was accepted and the date that acceptance has to be
argued again.

Carried and accepted are different numbers, and both are stated. A file saying
only what is accepted read "0 accepted findings" on a catalogue carrying 596.
Accepted is a subset of carried: accepting a finding records that it was looked
at, it does not take it out of the image — so the carried count includes what
the audit's ignore file removes from its own scan results (#310).

This file is committed, so its diff is the history of what the catalogue
delivers, and it carries no generation date: the same inputs produce the same
bytes, and a changed line means something actually changed.

Only the built-in catalogue is described here. Presets your own `presets.toml`
declares are yours, and CIDX makes no claim about them (guardrail 1).

An entry past its expiry date waives nothing until it is reviewed; `cidx
security vuln check` is what reports those, and `cidx security vuln prune`
reports the ones no catalogue image carries any more.

**21 images. 240 accepted HIGH/CRITICAL finding(s) across 17 of them.**

## What the images carry

The catalogue carries **1152** HIGH/CRITICAL findings, counted per image — the
same CVE on five images is five repins. They split into four populations:

| Population | Count | What it means |
| ---------- | ----- | ------------- |
| Go stdlib in a CLI binary | 107 | Exempt by class: it goes away when the publisher recompiles, and `net/http` is unreachable in a tool that opens no listener. |
| Kernel headers | 163 | Exempt by class: the kernel is the host's, not the container's. The scanner flags the headers package for its version string. |
| Fixed upstream | 727 | A fix exists. This is the images' age, not a decision — an exception must never be written for one. |
| **Needing triage** | **155** | No fix at any version, and not exempt. The only population an exception is the right instrument for. |

None of them is in CISA KEV. The highest EPSS score seen is 0.04. Both are reported
for a human to read; neither gates anything.

## Images

The **Base** column is the distribution the image is built on, as the scanners
report it. It is here because it decides whether the findings above can ever
go away: once a base stops being supported, its packages receive no further
updates and every finding on that image is permanent, however fresh the tag
is. `none` is an image with no distribution underneath it — a scratch or
static build — which is an answer, not a gap.

The date that support ends is deliberately **not** in this file. It is
relative to the day you read it and it comes from a third party, so it would
change these lines without anything changing about the catalogue — the same
reason there is no generation date. `cidx security baseline` prints it, and
the daily security audit reports it.

Added 2026-09-30, on the same footing: glibc (CVE-2026-19499): needs an application calling strfmon or strfmon_l with right-justified width padding into a small buffer; no tool here does. zlib (CVE-2026-85091): a heap overflow in the gzFile write path (gzprintf or gzwrite after a stalled non-blocking write); the tools here reach zlib through inflate and deflate, and none writes through gzFile on a non-blocking descriptor. docker/docker (GO-2026-4887): an AuthZ-plugin bypass on oversized request bodies, daemon-side code in the client library vendored here; the daemon is the host's. All are HIGH or CRITICAL with no fix at any version, EPSS at most 0.007, none in KEV (audit run 36565600041, 2026-09-29). Checked against the commands these presets run; re-argue if they start running the affected tool. Added 2026-09-30 (second audit of the day): libssl3t64 (CVE-2026-84782): an out-of-bounds read in OpenSSL's DTLS retransmission, so datagram TLS over UDP; the tools here speak TLS over TCP, a different code path, and none opens a DTLS connection. HIGH, no fix at any version, EPSS 0, not in KEV (audit run 36682383284, 2026-09-30). Added 2026-09-30 (third audit of the day): libssl3t64 (CVE-2026-72897, CVE-2026-84784): the first is on the TLS server side (a server switching SSL_CTX part-way through a handshake), the second a flood of the QUIC stack; no preset runs a TLS server or speaks QUIC, so neither code path is reached. HIGH, no fix at any version, EPSS 0, not in KEV (audit run 36683428551, 2026-09-30). |

| `ghcr.io/ansible/community-ansible-dev-tools:v26.7.1@sha256:4d4db3e75c48ce64763d26adbca58ff3f8b93a8ddae785373ac973b4f20a7d92` | CVE-2024-25621 | HIGH | accepted-risk | 2026-10-30 | runc, containerd, docker/docker and selinux are vendored into /usr/local/bin/kubectl, which no preset invokes; the vulnerable paths need a container to be run by that binary, and kubectl runs none (docker/docker's flaws are daemon-side handlers -- container archive API, docker cp, the AuthZ plugin -- absent from a client binary). Fixed versions exist at module level and reach us only when the image ships a rebuilt kubectl. Re-argued 2026-09-30 against audit run 36565600041 and a fresh scan of v26.9.0, the newest upstream tag: its kubectl still vendors runc 1.1.13, containerd 1.7.11, docker/docker 27.1.1 and selinux 1.12.0, so no image ships the fix. As decided 2026-08-22 for exactly this case, the treatment is now accepted-risk under the inert model rather than awaiting-upstream -- the blast radius, if inertness is wrong, includes the Docker socket and the Galaxy token -- rather than disabling seven presets over an uninvoked library. The review is a month out on purpose: at each one, scan the newest tag, and if an image has rebuilt kubectl, repin instead of renewing. |

A container has no fstab, runs as an unprivileged uid, and no preset here runs mount or nsenter. libsystemd0 (CVE-2026-16742): a systemd-homed local privilege escalation; no systemd runs in a container and nothing here talks to it. perl-base (CVE-2026-82560): CPU exhaustion formatting a crafted POD document; nothing here runs pod2text or Pod::Text. glibc (CVE-2026-19499): needs an application calling strfmon or strfmon_l with right-justified width padding into a small buffer; no tool here does. zlib (CVE-2026-85091): a heap overflow in the gzFile write path (gzprintf or gzwrite after a stalled non-blocking write); the tools here reach zlib through inflate and deflate, and none writes through gzFile on a non-blocking descriptor. All are HIGH or CRITICAL with no fix at any version, EPSS at most 0.007, none in KEV (audit run 36565600041, 2026-09-29). Checked against the commands these presets run; re-argue if they start running the affected tool. Added 2026-09-30 (second audit of the day): libssl3t64 (CVE-2026-84782): an out-of-bounds read in OpenSSL's DTLS retransmission, so datagram TLS over UDP; the tools here speak TLS over TCP, a different code path, and none opens a DTLS connection. HIGH, no fix at any version, EPSS 0, not in KEV (audit run 36682383284, 2026-09-30). Added 2026-09-30 (third audit of the day): libssl3t64 (CVE-2026-72897, CVE-2026-84784): the first is on the TLS server side (a server switching SSL_CTX part-way through a handshake), the second a flood of the QUIC stack; no preset runs a TLS server or speaks QUIC, so neither code path is reached. All are HIGH or CRITICAL with no fix at any version, EPSS at most 0.007, none in KEV (audit run 36565600041, 2026-09-29). Checked against the commands these presets run; re-argue if they start running the affected tool. Added 2026-09-30 (second audit of the day): libssl3t64 (CVE-2026-84782): an out-of-bounds read in OpenSSL's DTLS retransmission, so datagram TLS over UDP; the tools here speak TLS over TCP, a different code path, and none opens a DTLS connection. HIGH, no fix at any version, EPSS 0, not in KEV (audit run 36682383284, 2026-09-30). Added 2026-09-30 (third audit of the day): libssl3t64 (CVE-2026-72897, CVE-2026-84784): the first is on the TLS server side (a server switching SSL_CTX part-way through a handshake), the second a flood of the QUIC stack; no preset runs a TLS server or speaks QUIC, so neither code path is reached. HIGH, no fix at any version, EPSS 0, not in KEV (audit run 36683428551, 2026-09-30). |

Checked against the commands these presets run; re-argue if they start running the affected tool. HIGH, no fix at any version, EPSS 0, not in KEV (audit run 36682383284, 2026-09-30).
